notes.meaning: Jesus had already ordered the evil spirit to leave the man. The demon had seized him many times and broken strong iron chains, violently driving him out into lonely places. Jesus stepped in with divine authority to free this helpless man from terrible cruelty.

Jesus asked the demon for its name so everyone present could see the man's desperate condition. The evil spirit answered 'Legion,' which was the name of a Roman army unit made up of thousands of soldiers. This showed that a vast number of demons had taken control of the man.

The demons begged Jesus not to banish them into the Abyss, which means the bottomless pit of punishment. They knew Jesus had full authority over them and could send them to their final prison whenever He chose.

A large herd of pigs was feeding nearby on the hillside, and the demons begged to enter them instead. Evil spirits cannot harm even an animal without God's permission, and Jesus granted their request.

When the demons left the man and went into the pigs, the entire herd panicked and plunged down the steep hill into the lake, where they drowned. This sudden rush showed what the demons had always wanted to do to the man himself: utterly destroy him.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars suggest the man only believed himself possessed and needed to see the pigs stampede to feel truly convinced of his cure.

notes.meaning: The men herding the pigs saw the whole event happen right before their eyes and ran away in panic. They hurried into the town and the surrounding fields to tell everyone about the loss of the herd.

The local people came out to investigate what had taken place. They found the man who had been possessed sitting calmly at the feet of Jesus, wearing clothes and in his right mind, and the sight filled them with fear.
The people who had watched the miracle explained the details to the newcomers. They described how the tormented man had been completely delivered and restored to health.

Terrified by Jesus' great power and upset over the loss of their property, the whole crowd begged Jesus to leave their region. Jesus respected their wish, got back into the boat, and crossed back over the lake.

The man who had been set free pleaded with Jesus to let him come along with Him. While the others wanted Jesus gone, this man felt drawn to Him in gratitude, but Jesus sent him away for a special purpose.

Jesus told the man to return home and tell his family and neighbors how much God had done for him. The man obeyed immediately and announced through the whole town the wonderful things Jesus had done in his life.
When Jesus sailed back to the other side of the lake, a great crowd gave Him a warm welcome. Unlike the people He had just left, these Galileans had been eagerly waiting on the shore for His return.
A leader of the local synagogue named Jairus came through the crowd and bowed low at Jesus' feet. Putting aside his important position, he humbly begged Jesus to come to his home.
Jairus was desperate because his only daughter, who was about twelve years old, was dying. As Jesus set out with him, a massive crowd packed in close and crushed against Him from every side.
In the press of people was a woman who had suffered from chronic bleeding for twelve long years. She had spent all her money on doctors, but none of them had been able to cure her.
Feeling ashamed and unclean, she slipped quietly behind Jesus and touched the fringe of His outer robe. The very moment her fingers touched the cloth, her bleeding completely stopped.

differ.view: The woman's idea that touching the fringe of a coat could heal showed an imperfect faith mixed with superstition.
Her touch was an act of genuine faith in the real power of Jesus, not superstition.

notes.meaning: Jesus turned around and asked who had touched Him, but everyone near Him denied doing it. Peter spoke up to point out the obvious fact that the crowd was bumping and pushing against Him from all directions.

Jesus insisted that someone had deliberately reached out to Him, because He felt healing power go out from Him. Many people brushed against Him by accident, but only one touch drew upon His power through faith.

Realizing she could no longer stay hidden, the woman stepped forward trembling with awe and fell at Jesus' feet. Right in front of the whole crowd, she confessed why she had reached for Him and announced that she had been healed instantly.
Jesus spoke to her with deep tenderness, calling her 'Daughter.' He assured her that it was her faith that had brought her healing and told her to go forward in complete peace.

While Jesus was still comforting the woman, a messenger came from Jairus's house with crushing news. He told the father that the girl was already dead, so there was no point in bothering the Teacher any longer.
Jesus heard the messenger's report and immediately stepped in to encourage the grieving father. He told Jairus not to be afraid, but simply to keep trusting Him, and his daughter would be restored.

When Jesus reached the home, He kept the noisy crowd outside and took only Peter, John, James, and the girl's parents into the room. He chose these few witnesses so the grieving family would have peace and to prevent wild excitement.

Inside, family and mourners were weeping loudly and beating their breasts in deep sorrow. Jesus told them to stop crying because the child was not permanently gone, but only sleeping until He woke her.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars interpret Jesus' words literally, suggesting the girl had not actually died but had fallen into a deep trance or coma.

notes.meaning: The mourners mocked Jesus and laughed in His face because they were certain the girl was dead. Their sharp reaction actually served to prove that her death was real, leaving no doubt about the miracle that followed.
After putting the loud mourners outside, Jesus gently took the girl by the hand. He spoke with the firm authority of God, calling out for the child to get up.
Her spirit returned into her body, and she stood right up completely well. Jesus then told her parents to give her something to eat, which proved she was truly alive and restored to everyday life.
The girl's parents were completely overwhelmed with wonder and relief. Jesus instructed them not to spread what had happened, wanting to avoid unhelpful publicity and sensational crowds.
